IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p206/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p206/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p206/r2.claim: God can restore even the tiny finger joints and assemble them precisely; whoever can do that can more easily gather the larger bones.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p206/r2.anchor: فقال: بلى، فاعلموا أنا نقدر على رد السلاميات على صغرها، ونؤلف بينها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p206/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p206/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p206/r3.claim: He illustrates the proof with a challenge about threading a bitter gourd, answered by an even finer comparison involving mustard.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p206/r3.anchor: مثل هذا رجل قلت له: أتراك تقدر على أن تؤلف هذا الحنظل في خيط؟ فيقول لك: نعم وبين الخردل.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r1.speaker: ابن الأثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r1.claim: Ibn al-Athir defines banān as the fingers or their tips; banāna is the singular.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r1.anchor: البنان الأصابع، وقيل أطرافها، واحدتها بنانة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says banān are the fingers as the body’s extremities and last parts to form, or that God can restore their finely detailed joints exactly as before.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r2.anchor: ذكر الأطراف على أنها أصابع الإنسان التى هى أطرافه وآخر ما يتم من خلقه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r3.claim: Another reported reading is that God can gather human bones yet make fingers and toes into a single hoof-like piece, preventing ordinary dexterity.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r3.anchor: عظام الإنسان - ونحن قادرون على أن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan calls al-Zamakhshari’s wording affected; he reads the verse as restoring the fingers, among the most finely divided bones, at resurrection.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r4.anchor: ورأى أبو حيان فى قول الزمخشرى تكلفا وتنميق ألفاظ

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and most exegetes say the fingers could be made into one lump or bone during life, diminishing their usefulness; the author says the resurrection reading is the clear intent.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p566/r5.anchor: وهذا القول فيه توعد. والمعنى الأول هو الظاهر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p61/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p61/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p61/r3.claim: The greater Judgment is reflected by conscience as a lesser judgment: people commit evil before an inward divine witness that rebukes them despite their excuses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p61/r3.anchor: if a person does some evil, he does not do it in hiding; he does so at the very doors of the divine court of justice

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r3.claim: Verses 1-6 swear by Judgment and cite the reproaching soul as evidence; deniers contradict their own conscience when demanding haste and calling resurrection impossible, like a brazen thief before a judge.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r3.anchor: The reproaching soul in man is also presented as a proof of that Day

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p344/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p344/r10.speaker: الجمهور وابن أبي عبلة وابن السميفع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p344/r10.claim: The majority read qadirin in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase; Ibn Abi ʿAbla and Ibn al-Sumayfi read qadirun, ‘We are able.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p344/r10.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: قادرين بالنصب على الحال من الضمير الذي في الفعل المقدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p344/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p344/r11.speaker: ابن عباس والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p344/r11.claim: They explain ‘make his fingertips even’ as making the hand’s bones a single piece during earthly life, reducing its usefulness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p344/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والجمهور: المعنى نجعلها في حياته هذه بضعة، أو عظما واحدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p344/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p344/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p344/r12.claim: The apparent meaning is God’s ability to reassemble even the most dispersed and finely divided fingertip bones at resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p344/r12.anchor: والمعنى الأول هو الظاهر والمقصود من رصف الكلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-20/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-20/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-20/r2.claim: God can join the tiny finger joints as they were, so larger bones are easier; or the fingertips specifically are mentioned a fortiori. A nominative reading says ‘We are capable.’
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:9-20/r2.anchor: { قدرين على أن نسوى بنانه } بجمع سلامياته وضم بعضها إلى بعض كما كانت مع صغرها ولطافتها فكيف بكبار العظام

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p205/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p205/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p205/r3.claim: Bala qadirin omits the governing verb, supplied by grammarians as We gather them while able; this omission also matches haste. Specific finger-bone shaping sits beside gathering bones, while general shaping appears with general creation later.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p205/r3.anchor: وملاحظة أخرى في هذا التعبير، وهي أنه حذف منه عامل الحال، فقال: {بلى قَادِرِينَ} ولم يذكر عامله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p237/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p237/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p237/r1.claim: The explicit bala qadirin affirms finger-shaping but omits its verb and circumstantial subject; the complete, emphatic question about reviving the dead marks its greater rhetorical weight.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p237/r1.anchor: فدلَّ ذلك على الفرق بين المقامين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p237/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p237/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p237/r3.claim: Haste appears through omitted elements: the oath's answer, the governing verb of qadirin, the antecedent of the tongue pronoun, and the unstated subject of balaghat.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p237/r3.anchor: فمن مراعاة جانب العجلة: 1- حذف جواب القسم الذي افتتحت به السورة وهو {لاَ أُقْسِمُ}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r9.claim: It pairs divine power to shape fingertips with power to revive the dead, using direct affirmation for the first and an interrogative affirmation for the second.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r9.anchor: وذكرت نوعين من القدرة: القدرة على تسوية البنان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r1.claim: The surah contrasts restricted, partial shaping of fingertips with the unrestricted, general shaping of creation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r1.anchor: وذكر نوعين من التسوية: تسوية جزئية مقيدة وهي تسوية البنان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p240/r4.claim: God is described with plural forms such as We are able, We gather, and We shape, as well as singular forms such as He created and proportioned.

THALABI:v10p82/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p82/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p82/r6.claim: Qadirin is accusative as a shift from the verb gather, while Ibn Abi Ghila reads the nominative qadirun with an implied we; the meaning is that God can reassemble even fingertips.
THALABI:v10p82/r6.anchor: ثم قال سبحانه: بلى قادرين أي نقدر استقبال صرف إلى الحال

THALABI:v10p82/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p82/r7.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v10p82/r7.claim: Al-Farra says the accusative leaves the gathering clause to mean that God is able to do more than gathering bones.
THALABI:v10p82/r7.anchor: قال الفراء: قادرين نصب على الخروج من نجمع كأنك قلت في الكلام: أيحسب أن لن يقوى عليك

THALABI:v10p82/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p82/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p82/r8.claim: God can restore the fingertips and keep the fingers distinct, enabling grasp and movement instead of making the limbs like hooves or a donkey's hoof.
THALABI:v10p82/r8.anchor: على أن نسوي بنانه أنامله فيجعل أصابع يديه ورجليه شيئا واحد كخف البعير، أو كظلف الخنزير

THALABI:v10p82/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p82/r9.speaker: القبيسي
THALABI:v10p82/r9.claim: Al-Qubaysi argues that restoring tiny finger bones demonstrates God's ability to gather larger bones, like threading small grains onto a string.
THALABI:v10p82/r9.anchor: وقال القبيسي: ظن الكافر أن الله لا يبعث الموتى ولا يقدر على جمع العظام البالية

ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r15.claim: Balā affirms a preceding negative by reversing it—“yes, indeed”—whereas naʿam or lā can simply repeat the negative; here the implied answer is that God will certainly gather the bones.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r16.claim: The implied verb “We gather” supplies the sense of balā, and “being able” grammatically describes the implied subject of that verb.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r16.anchor: mukabil بـَلٰى نَجْمَع demektir. {قَٰدِرِينَ} de mukadder

ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r17.claim: God can restore not only large bones but every detail, down to the fingertips; their fine construction signals the remarkable subtlety of bodily creation.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r17.anchor: en ince teşkîlâtına varıncaya kadar hepsini, hatta gövdesinin, etrafının en ince uçları olan

ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r18.claim: Hands symbolize power and accomplish people’s most important work; fingers and fingertips carry that agency and astonishing touch sensitivity, so reconstructing them encompasses the works and artifacts produced by a person.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r18.anchor: Parmaklarda ve parmak uçlarında öyle acîb bir sanat

ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r19.claim: The author illustrates fingertip sensitivity with a person distinguishing materials and sacks in a dark shop by tapping with a cane; tactile nerves register fine differences in vibration.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r19.anchor: Karanlık bir gecede meselâ bir kiler veya bir dükkânda gezinirken elinizdeki bir baston ile şuraya buraya dürttükçe

ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r20.claim: God can gather all human characteristics in one cell, just as a tiny particle of the tailbone is said to contain the person’s features.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#2/r20.anchor: bir zerre içinde bir insanın bütün hususiyetlerini toplar.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأتميميامرةوقيسياأخرى|وإ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأتميميامرةوقيسياأخرى|وإ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكأتميميامرةوقيسياأخرى|وإ.claim: Sibawayh, citing Yunus, reads بلى قادرين as an accusative dependent on the elided verb بلى نجمعها قادرين.

NAHHAS:v5p79/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p79/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p79/r1.claim: One proposed parse supplies “we are able,” then treats qadirin as accusative after converting the verb to an active participle; the verse’s qadirin is in the accusative.
NAHHAS:v5p79/r1.anchor: قادرين في موضع نصب وفي نصبه أقوال منها أنه قيل التقدير بلى نقدر فلما حول نقدر إلى قادرين نصب

NAHHAS:v5p79/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p79/r2.speaker: الفرزدق
NAHHAS:v5p79/r2.claim: The cited line uses “nor one departing” as an accusative participle in a construction understood as “nor may he depart.”
NAHHAS:v5p79/r2.anchor: كما قال الفرزدق ( على حلفة لا أشتم الدهر مسلما … ولا خارجا من في زور كلام )

NAHHAS:v5p79/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p79/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p79/r3.claim: Nahhas rejects deriving the participle’s case from the former verb: each construction has its own syntax; he prefers taking the poem’s “departing” as coordinated with the syntactic position of “I do not curse.”
NAHHAS:v5p79/r3.anchor: وهذا خطأ لأن لكل إعرابه تقول جاءني زيد يضحك وجاءني زيد ضاحكا ومررت برجل يضحك وبرجل ضاحك ولا خارجا معطوف على موضع لا أشتم قال أبو جعفر هذا أصح ما قيل فيه

NAHHAS:v5p79/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p79/r4.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p79/r4.claim: Al-Farra supplies “rather, we are powerful to do that,” with qadirin as the circumstantial accusative.
NAHHAS:v5p79/r4.anchor: وقيل التقدير بلى نقوى على ذلك قادرين هذا قول الفراء

NAHHAS:v5p79/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p79/r5.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v5p79/r5.claim: Sibawayh construes the phrase as “rather, We gather it, being able”; al-Farra’s account is derived from this.
NAHHAS:v5p79/r5.anchor: وقال سيبويه أي بلى نجمعها قادرين وقول الفراء مستخرج من هذا

NAHHAS:v5p79/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p79/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p79/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says God could make the fingertips one undifferentiated part, like a camel’s hoof or donkey’s hoof, preventing human eating by hand; God favored humanity.
NAHHAS:v5p79/r6.anchor: ومن حسن ما قيل فيه قول ابن عباس نحن نقدر أن نجعل بنانه شيئا واحدا كخف البعير وحافر الحمار

NAHHAS:v5p79/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p79/r7.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v5p79/r7.claim: Hasan says the fingers could be made uniform, without beauty and scarcely useful.
NAHHAS:v5p79/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن كنا نقدر أن نجعل أصابعه قدرا واحدا ولا يكون لها حسن ولا يكاد ينتفع بها

NAHHAS:v5p79/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p79/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p79/r8.claim: Banan is the plural of banāna, a fingertip.
NAHHAS:v5p79/r8.anchor: وبنان جمع بنانة ومن حسن ما قيل فيه قول ابن عباس

SAMIN-DURR:75:4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:4/r1.claim: بلى affirms what follows the negation contained in the interrogative.
SAMIN-DURR:75:4/r1.anchor: قوله: { بلى } إيجاب لما بعد النفي المنسحب عليه الاستفهام.

SAMIN-DURR:75:4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:4/r2.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:75:4/r2.claim: The common reading has قادرين in the accusative; the preferred analysis makes it circumstantial to the implied جمعها, supplied by the response particle.
SAMIN-DURR:75:4/r2.anchor: أشهرهما: أنه منصوب على الحال من فاعل الفعل المقدر المدلول عليه بحرف الجواب

SAMIN-DURR:75:4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:4/r3.claim: A less clear alternative treats قادرين as the predicate of an omitted كان: ‘we were able’ from the beginning.
SAMIN-DURR:75:4/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنه منصوب على خبر " كان " مضمرة أي: بلى كنا قادرين في الابتداء، وهذا ليس بواضح

SAMIN-DURR:75:4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:4/r4.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة وابن السميفع
SAMIN-DURR:75:4/r4.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAblah and Ibn al-Sumayfa read nominative قادرون, as predicate of an implicit subject.
SAMIN-DURR:75:4/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة وابن السميفع " قادرون " رفعا على خبر ابتداء مضمر

ZAJJAJ:v5p251/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p251/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p251/r6.claim: The meaning is, ‘Yes, We shall gather you, being able to restore even your fingertips as they were.’
ZAJJAJ:v5p251/r6.anchor: المعنى: بلى لنجمعنكم قادرين، المعنى أقسم بيوم القيامة والنفس اللوامة لنجمعنها قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه.

ZAJJAJ:v5p251/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p251/r7.speaker: جاء في التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v5p251/r7.claim: A tafsir says the fingertips could be made like a camel's hoof.
ZAJJAJ:v5p251/r7.anchor: وجاء في التفسير بلى نقدر على أن نجعله كخف البعير.

ZAJJAJ:v5p251/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p251/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p251/r8.claim: He prefers the reading that God gathers the bones and can restore even the small fingertip bones to their original form after decay.
ZAJJAJ:v5p251/r8.anchor: والذي هو أشكل بجمع العظام بلى نجمعها قادرين، على تسوية بنانه على ما كانت، وإن قل عظامها وصغرت وبلغ منها البلى.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p565/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p565/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p565/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses banan as the fingertips and cites Antara's line about warriors holding reins by their fingers.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p565/r1.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: أطراف الأصابع. وشاهده قول عنترة العبسى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p565/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p565/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p565/r2.claim: Banan is the plural or collective form related to banana and denotes fingers or their tips; the lexicon notes it can mean a single finger.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p565/r2.anchor: البَنان واحدته بنانة، وهى الأصابع أو أطرافها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p565/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p565/r6.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله بن عمرو الأنصاري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p565/r6.claim: Jabir ibn Abdullah ibn Amr al-Ansari said he recognized his father, martyred at Uhud, only by his fingertips.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p565/r6.anchor: وفي حديث جابر، بن عبد الله بن عمرو الأنصارى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p565/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p565/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p565/r7.claim: The Qur'an uses banan only in the al-Anfal battle verse and the resurrection passage in al-Qiyama.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r1.claim: God will gather the bones after they have disintegrated and scattered in seas, deserts, and wherever they may be.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r1.anchor: أين جمعها بعد تفرقها ورجوعها رميما ورفاتا في بطون البحار وفسيحات القفار وحيثما كانت

ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r2.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r2.claim: Sībawayh takes qādirīn as a circumstantial accusative from the subject of the implied verb after balā.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r2.anchor: فقادرين حال من فاعل الفعل المقدر بعد بلى وهو قول سيبويه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r3.claim: An alternative makes qādirīn the predicate of kāna, meaning: were We capable at the beginning but not of returning them? Al-Ālūsī dismisses this reading as untenable.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r3.anchor: وقيل منصوب على أنه خبر كان أيبلى كنا قادرين في البدء أفلا نقدر في الإعادة وهو كما ترى

ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r4.speaker: مكي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r4.claim: Makkī says the word occupies the place of the verb naqdِr and is therefore accusative; al-Ālūsī reports the objection that this would wrongly license an accusative circumstantial form after a noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r4.anchor: حكاه مكي وقال أنه بعيد من الصواب يلزم عليه نصب قائم في قولك مررت برجل قائم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r5.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة وابن السمقيع
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Ibn al-Sumayqiʿ read qādirūn in the nominative, as an independent assertion that God is capable.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة وابن السمقيع قادرون أي نحن قادرون

ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r6.claim: Banān is a collective noun with singular banāna.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r6.anchor: هي اسم جنس جمع يواحده بنانة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r7.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r7.claim: Al-Rāghib glosses banān as fingers and links the name to their role in indicating or communicating what a person intends.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r7.anchor: وفسرها الراغب بالأصابع ثم قال قيل سميت بذلك لأن بها صلاح الأحوال التي يمكن للإنسان أن يبين بها ما يريد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r8.speaker: القاموس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r8.claim: Al-Qāmūs defines banān as fingers or their tips.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r8.anchor: وفي القاموس البنان الأصابع أو أطرافها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r9.claim: One reading is that God will gather all the bones and restore them to their original arrangement, including fingers as the final part completing the form.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r9.anchor: فالمعنى نجمع العظام قادرين على تأليف جمعها وإعادتها إلى التركيب الأول وإلى أن نسوي أصابعه التي هي أطرافه وأخر ما يتم به خلقه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds it especially apt that God can restore the delicate phalanges exactly as before, with no loss or variation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r10.anchor: أو على أن نسوي ونضم سلامياته على صغرها ولطافتها بعضها إلى بعض كما كانت أولا من غير نقصان ولا تفاوت

ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r11.claim: Mentioning fingers highlights either the complete bodily gathering or, especially, the greater proof that restoring tiny, delicate parts entails restoring larger bones all the more.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r11.anchor: والوجه الأول من المعنى يدل على تصوير الجمع وأنه لا تفاوت بين الإعادة والبدء في الاشتمال على جميع الأجزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r12.claim: The second interpretation makes the point that if God can gather the finest parts, He is even more able to gather the rest.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r12.anchor: الثاني يدل على تحقيق الجمع التام فإنه إذا قدر على جمع الألطف إلا بعد عادة عن الإعادة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد وعكرمة والضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk report that God can make the fingers of hands and feet uniform like a camel’s pad or donkey’s hoof, removing their articulated utility.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r13.anchor: وروي هذا من ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد وعكرمة والضحاك

ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r14.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r14.claim: Abū Ḥayyān attributes to the majority an interpretation in which the fingers are made alike in this life; he says it then threatens loss of their useful dexterity, but al-Ālūsī says this departs from the apparent resurrection context.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r14.anchor: وأبو حيان حكى هذا عن الجمهور لكن قيد التسوية فيه بكونها في الدنيا وقال أن في الكلام عليه نوعدا ثم تعقب ذلك بأنه خلاف الظاهر المقصود من سوق الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r15.claim: The affirmative reply, omitted oath response, emphatic questioning about humanity, and following circumstantial phrase jointly intensify the certainty of resurrection and censure heedlessness.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p137#2/r15.anchor: من المبالغات في تحقيق المطلوب وتفخيمه وتهجين المعرض على الاستعداد له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r1.claim: The passage was revealed about ʿAdī ibn Rabīʿa, who asked the Prophet about the Resurrection and declared he would not believe even if he saw it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r1.anchor: نزلت في عدي بن ربيعة، حليف بني زهرة، ختن الأخنس بن شريق الثقفي،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r2.claim: The Prophet used to pray for protection from the two bad neighbors, meaning ʿAdī and al-Akhnaṣ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r2.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: اللهم اكفني جاري السوء، يعني: عديا والأخنس.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r3.claim: Some say bones stand for the person, since bones are the soul's frame and the body is not formed evenly without them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r3.anchor: قيل: ذكر العظام وأراد نفسه لأن العظام قالب النفس لا يستوي الخلق إلا باستوائها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r4.claim: The objection echoes the denier's question in Yā Sīn about who can revive decayed bones.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو خارج على قول المنكر أو يجمع الله العظام كقوله: "قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم" (يس-78)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r5.claim: Bala means that God is able to gather the bones and do more than that, including making the fingertips even.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r5.anchor: بلى قادرين} أي نقدر، استقبال صرف إلى الحال،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r6.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ parses qādirīn as accusative departing from najmaʿ, in the sense of being able to do more than the challenged task.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r6.anchor: قال الفراء "قادرين" نصب على الخروج من نجمع، كما تقول في الكلام أتحسب أن لا نقوى عليك؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r7.claim: Most commentators say God could make the fingers and toes one piece like a camel's hoof or donkey's hoof, preventing grasping and fine work such as writing and sewing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r7.anchor: أصابع يديه ورجليه شيئا واحدا كخف البعير وحافر الحمار، فلا يرتفق بها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r8.speaker: الزجاج وابن قتيبة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj and Ibn Qutayba explain that God can reassemble tiny phalanges into fingertips; assembling small bones proves He can assemble larger ones.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p280/r8.anchor: وقال الزجاج وابن قتيبة: معناه: ظن الكافر أنا لا نقدر على جمع عظامه، بلى نقدر على أن نعيد السلاميات

DURR-FULL:v8p342/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p342/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p342/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says God could make the fingertips into a palm with no fingers.
DURR-FULL:v8p342/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس {بلى قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه} قال: نجعلها كفا ليس فيه أصابع

DURR-FULL:v8p343/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p343/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p343/r1.claim: God could have made people with camel or donkey hooves, but instead gave them a sound, beautiful form with hands that grip and open.
DURR-FULL:v8p343/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس {بلى قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه} قال: لو شاء لجعله كخف البعير أو كحافر الحمار

DURR-FULL:v8p343/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p343/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p343/r2.claim: Mujahid says God could make people's feet like a camel's hoof, preventing them from working with them.
DURR-FULL:v8p343/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد {على أن نسوي بنانه} قال: يجعل رجليه كخف البعير فلا يعمل بها شيئا

DURR-FULL:v8p343/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p343/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p343/r3.claim: Ikrima says God could return the limbs to the useless form of a camel's hoof.
DURR-FULL:v8p343/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة {على أن نسوي بنانه} قال: إن شاء رده مثل خف البعير حتى لا ينتفع

DURR-FULL:v8p343/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p343/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p343/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says God could make feet, or hands and feet, like a camel's hoof so they could not be used.
DURR-FULL:v8p343/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك {على أن نسوي بنانه} قال: يجعل رجليه كخف البعير فلا يعمل بهما شيئا

DURR-FULL:v8p343/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p343/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p343/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says God honored human eating by giving people hands rather than hooves, so they eat and fend off the ground with their hands while other animals use their mouths.
DURR-FULL:v8p343/r5.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ هذه الآية {بلى قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه} فقال: إن الله أعف مطعم ابن آدم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r1.claim: A good stop follows bala, then qadirin begins the next clause: Yes, We will assemble them, fully able to do so.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r1.anchor: بلى وقف حسن ثم يبتدأ قادرين على معنى بلى نجمعها قادرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r2.claim: Qadirin may instead be accusative by repeating bala, with the sense that they should reckon God able to restore the fingertips.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r2.anchor: ويصلح نصب قادرين على التكرير بل فليحسبنا قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r3.claim: The majority say God could make the fingers of hands and feet into a single camel-like pad or donkey hoof, removing the ability to do delicate work such as writing and sewing.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r3.anchor: أحدهما أن نجعل أصابع يديه ورجليه شيئا واحد كخف البعير وحافر الحمار فيعدم الاتفاق بالأعمال اللطيفة كالكتابة والخياطة هذا قول الجمهور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba and al-Zajjaj say God can restore the fingertips as they were despite their small bones; whoever gathers small bones can more readily gather large ones.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r4.anchor: والثاني نقدر على أن نسوي بنانه كما كانت وإن صغرت عظامها ومن قدر على جمع صغار العظام كان على جمع كبارها أقدر هذا قول ابن قتيبة والزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r5.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi refers readers to his explanation of banan at al-Anfal 8:12.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p417/r5.anchor: وقد بينا معنى البنان في الأنفال 12

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p276/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p276/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير والعوفي ومجاهد وعكرمة والحسن وقتادة والضحاك وابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p276/r5.claim: These authorities explain the verse as God’s ability to turn human fingers into a hoof or cloven hoof.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p276/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أن نجعله (3) خفا أو حافرا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p276/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p276/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p276/r6.claim: Al-Tabari’s rationale for the hoof reading is that God could have made people that way in this world.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p276/r6.anchor: ووجهه ابن جرير بأنه تعالى لو شاء لجعل ذلك في الدنيا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p276/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p276/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p276/r7.claim: The apparent syntax makes “able” circumstantial to “gather”; God can gather bones and make fingertips level.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p276/r7.anchor: والظاهر من الآية أن قوله: {قادرين} حال من قوله: {نجمع} أي: أيظن الإنسان أنا لا نجمع عظامه؟ بلى سنجمعها قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p276/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p276/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة والزجاج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p276/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba and al-Zajjaj understand the fingertips to be made even and smooth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p276/r8.anchor: مستوية. وهذا معنى قول ابن قتيبة، والزجاج.

JISHUMI:v10p7175/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7175/r7.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
JISHUMI:v10p7175/r7.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads qādirūn in the nominative with wāw, implying omitted نحن.
JISHUMI:v10p7175/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة: بلى قادرون بالواو والرفع، على تقدير: بلى نحن قادرون.

JISHUMI:v10p7175/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7175/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7175/r11.claim: One analysis omits the oath's answer, understood as swearing resurrection will occur; another makes لنجمعنها قادرين the answer.
JISHUMI:v10p7175/r11.anchor: لا أقسم قسم، وجوابه قيل: محذوف، وتقديره: أقسم بالقيامة إنه كائن، وقيل: جواب القسم

JISHUMI:v10p7175/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7175/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7175/r12.claim: Another analysis takes لنجمعنها قادرين as the oath response.
JISHUMI:v10p7175/r12.anchor: وقيل: جواب القسم، أي: لنجمعنها قادرين.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r12.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r12.claim: Al-Akhfash treats balā as completing the preceding question: indeed, God will gather the bones.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r12.anchor: أنه تمام قوله ( أن لن نجمع عظامه ) أي بلى نجمعها , قاله الأخفش

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r13.claim: A second construction takes balā as the start of a new emphatic exclamation after the first statement ends.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r13.anchor: أنها استئناف بعد تمام الأول بالتعجب بلى قادرين

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r14.speaker: جرير بن عبد العزيز
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r14.claim: Jarir ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz says God can restore the joints and remake the person for resurrection.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r14.anchor: بلى قادرين على أن نسوي مفاصله ونعيدها للبعث خلقا جديدا , قاله جرير بن عبد العزيز

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r15.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatada say God could turn the hand into a donkey's hoof or camel's foot, leaving it unable to eat or work with its hand.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r15.anchor: حافر حمار أو خف بعير , فلا يأكل إلا بفيه , ولا يعمل بيده شيئا , قاله ابن عباس وقتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r16.claim: The verse answers denial of bodily resurrection by asserting God's ability to re-form even the fine details of the body.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p150#2/r16.anchor: بلى قادرين على أن نسوي مفاصله ونعيدها للبعث خلقا جديدا

MUQATIL:75:1-7/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:1-7/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:1-7/r8.claim: God can restore even the fingers, joining them to the palm and reshaping them like a camel's hoof, useless for grasping.
MUQATIL:75:1-7/r8.anchor: يعني على أن نلحق الأصابع بالراحة ونسويه حتى نجعله مثل خف البعير

MUQATIL:75:1-7/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:1-7/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:1-7/r9.claim: Muqatil says this verse was revealed about Adi ibn Rabi'a and al-Akhnas ibn Shariq.
MUQATIL:75:1-7/r9.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في عدي بن ربيعة والأخنس بن شريق

BURSEVI:v10p189/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p189/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p189/r6.claim: Some deny resurrection from doubt, but God's ability to revive is certain to a reflective reasoner; the affirmative bala answers the denial by affirming that He will gather them.
BURSEVI:v10p189/r6.anchor: ودل هذا الإنكار على إنه ناشىء من الشبهة وذلك بالنسبة إلى البعض والله قار على الإحياء لا شبهة في بالنسبة إلى القال المتفكر المستدل

BURSEVI:v10p189/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p189/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p189/r7.claim: Qadirin is a circumstantial accusative affirming the implied subject of the estimated verb 'We gather them' after bala.
BURSEVI:v10p189/r7.anchor: فهو حال مؤكدة من الضمير المستكن في تجمع المقدر بعد بلى

BURSEVI:v10p189/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p189/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p189/r8.claim: God can collect and restore even the tiny phalanges of fingers, so restoring the larger bones is easier still.
BURSEVI:v10p189/r8.anchor: أي نجمع سلامياته ونضم بعضها إلى بعض كما كانت مع صغرها ولطافتها فكيف بكبار العظام

BURSEVI:v10p189/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p189/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p189/r9.claim: Salami is a plural for the small bones of the hand and foot, on the pattern of habara.
BURSEVI:v10p189/r9.anchor: وهو جمع سلامي كحبارى وهي العظام الصغار ي اليد والرجل

BURSEVI:v10p189/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p189/r10.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p189/r10.claim: A hadith says every joint of a person owes charity each day the sun rises, in any form of speech, action, or wealth.
BURSEVI:v10p189/r10.anchor: وفي الحديث كلا سلامي من الناس عليه صدقة كل يوم تطلع فيه الشمس أي على صاحبه صدقة من أي أنواع الصدقة

BURSEVI:v10p189/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p189/r11.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v10p189/r11.claim: Al-Qamus defines banan as the fingers or their tips.

BURSEVI:v10p189/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p189/r12.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p189/r12.claim: Al-Raghib says banan is named for the fingertips because they let a person put affairs in order and accomplish what he wants; the verse singles it out for that practical function.
BURSEVI:v10p189/r12.anchor: قال الراغب البنان الأصابع قيل سميت بذلك لأن بها إصلاح الأحوال

BURSEVI:v10p189/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p189/r13.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p189/r13.claim: Al-Raghib also cites the command to strike every fingertip to illustrate that the fingers are used to fight and defend.
BURSEVI:v10p189/r13.anchor: قال الراغب البنان الأصابع قيل سميت بذلك لأن بها إصلاح الأحوال

BURSEVI:v10p189/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p189/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p189/r14.claim: Banan may also be the fingertips, the last and smallest parts to be formed; it is singular in form but collective in meaning, like tamr, and connotes both smallness and extremity.
BURSEVI:v10p189/r14.anchor: أو المعنى على نسوى أصابعه التي هي أطرافه وآخر ما يتم به خلفه فالبنان مفرد اللفظ مجموع المعنى كالتمر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p299#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p299#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p299#5/r1.claim: “Yes indeed” affirms what the preceding negation denied: God will gather the bones.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p299#5/r1.anchor: أوجبت ما بعد النفي أي بلى نجمعها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p299#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p299#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p299#5/r2.claim: “Able” is a circumstantial accusative describing the implicit subject of “We gather.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p299#5/r2.anchor: حال من الضمير في نجمع أي نجمعها قادرين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p299#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p299#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p299#5/r3.claim: God can restore the fingertips exactly as in life, without loss or difference despite their smallness; how much more can He restore the larger bones.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p299#5/r3.anchor: أصابعه كما كانت في الدنيا بلا نقصان وتفاوت مع صغرها فكيف بكبار العظام

QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r14.claim: Al-Qurtubi marks a good pause after bala, then starts qadirin.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r14.anchor: { بلى } وقف حسن ثم تبتديء { قادرين }.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r15.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r15.claim: Sibawayh construes qadirin as a circumstantial accusative: ‘We gather them, being capable,’ with an implicit verb.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r15.anchor: قال سيبويه: على معنى نجمعها قادرين، ف «قادرين» حال من الفاعل المضمر في الفعل المحذوف

QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r16.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r16.claim: Al-Farraʾ construes the accusative as an explanatory continuation of najmaʿ, meaning able and powerful to do more.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r16.anchor: قال الفراء: «قادرين» نصب على الخروج من «نجمع»

QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r17.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r17.claim: Al-Farraʾ also allows an accusative by repetition, as if the sense were ‘Indeed, let us consider ourselves capable.’
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r17.anchor: وقال أيضا: يصلح نصبه على التكرير أي «بلى» فليحسبنا قادرين.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r18.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r18.claim: An alternative supplies ‘We were capable’ from the beginning, which the polytheists themselves acknowledged.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r18.anchor: وقيل: المضمر كنا أي كنا قادرين في الابتداء، وقد اعترف به المشركون.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r19.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة وابن السميقع
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r19.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla and Ibn al-Sumayqa read qadirun in the nominative, understood as ‘we are capable.’
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r19.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة وابن السميقع «بلى قادرون» بتأويل نحن قادرون.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r20.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r20.claim: Banan means fingers in Arabic, and its singular is banana.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:3-4/r20.anchor: البنان عند العرب: الأصابع، واحدها بنانة قال النابغة

QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r1.claim: Al-Nabigha's verse compares delicate fingertips with anʿam.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r1.anchor: بمخضب رخص كأن بنانه عنم يكاد من اللطافة يعقد

QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r2.speaker: عنترة
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r2.claim: ʿAntara's verse likewise uses banan for fingers, describing them joined to a sword.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r2.anchor: وقال عنترة: وأن الموت طوع يدي إذا ما وصلت بنانها بالهندواني

QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r3.claim: Mentioning fingertips draws attention to the remaining body parts; fingertips are singled out because they are the smallest bones.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r3.anchor: فنبه بالبنان على بقية الأعضاء. وأيضا فإنها أصغر العظام، فخصها بالذكر لذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r4.speaker: القتبي والزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r4.claim: Al-Qutaybi and al-Zajjaj say that although deniers thought God could not gather bones, He can restore tiny finger joints; whoever can do that can gather larger bones all the more.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r4.anchor: قال القتبي والزجاج: وزعموا أن الله لا يبعث الموتى ولا يقدر على جمع العظام فقال الله تعالى: بلى قادرين

QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وعامة المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and most exegetes say God could fuse fingers into an animal's pad, hoof, or cloven hoof, leaving a person unable to act; instead He separated them for grasping.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وعامة المفسرين: المعنى: «على أن نسوي بنانه» أي نجعل أصابع يديه ورجليه شيئا واحدا كخف البعير

QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r6.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says God gave people fingers to extend and curl; if He joined them, a person could only traverse the earth on his palms.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r6.anchor: وكان الحسن يقول: جعل لك أصابع فأنت تبسطهن، وتقبضهن بهن، ولو شاء الله لجمعهن فلم تتق الأرض إلا بكفيك.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r7.claim: Another view says God could restore a person in an animal's form, so restoring the original human form is surely possible; it is likened to 56:60–61.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r7.anchor: وقيل: أي نقدر أن نعيد الإنسان في هيئة البهائم، فكيف في صورته التي كان عليها

QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the first interpretation best fits the passage.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:4-6/r8.anchor: قلت: والتأويل الأول أشبه بمساق الآية. والله أعلم.

STUDYQURAN:75:4/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:4/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:75:4/r1.claim: God can resurrect a person exactly as He first created him.
STUDYQURAN:75:4/r1.anchor: This verse is said to mean, “We are able to create him again precisely as we created him the first time”

QUSHAYRI:v3p368/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p368/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p368/r8.claim: Qādirīn is accusative as a circumstantial expression: God is able at that time to restore the fingertips.
QUSHAYRI:v3p368/r8.anchor: نصب على الحال ؛ أي بلى ، نسوي بنانه في الوقت قادرين ، ونقدر

QUSHAYRI:v3p368/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p368/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p368/r9.claim: God can make the person's fingers and toes one form, like a camel's hoof or a sheep's cloven hoof; if this is possible, resurrection is certainly possible.
QUSHAYRI:v3p368/r9.anchor: ونقدر أي نجعل أصابع يديه ورجليه شيئا واحدا كخف البعير وظلف الشاة . . فكيف لا نقدر على إعادته

TAB-FULL:v23p471/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r1.claim: God can do more than reassemble the bones: He can make the fingers one blunt piece like a camel's or donkey's hoof, preventing grasping and handling, though He fashioned dexterous fingers beautifully.
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r1.anchor: بفيه كسائر البهائم، ولكنه فرق أصابع يديه

TAB-FULL:v23p471/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God could have made the fingers into a hoof.
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r2.anchor: قال لي ابن عباس: سل، فقلت

TAB-FULL:v23p471/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r3.claim: Another Ibn ʿAbbās report says He could make the palm a mass like a camel's hoof.
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {بلى قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه}

TAB-FULL:v23p471/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is also reported to explain the phrase as making the fingers into a hoof.
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {بلى قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه}

TAB-FULL:v23p471/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r5.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r5.claim: ʿIkrima says God could have made the fingers like a camel's or donkey's hoof.
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r5.anchor: عن النضر، عن عكرمة، {على أن نسوي بنانه}

TAB-FULL:v23p471/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God made a hand with fingers that close and open, could have joined them, and fashioned humans beautifully.
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r6.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {بلى قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه}

TAB-FULL:v23p471/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r7.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r7.claim: ʿIkrima, when asked, answers that God could have made the hand like a camel's hoof.
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r7.anchor: وسئل عكرمة فقال: لو شاء لجعلها كخف البعير

TAB-FULL:v23p471/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r8.claim: Mujāhid identifies the fingers here as the feet, which could be made like a camel's hoof and rendered useless for work.
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {على أن نسوي بنانه}

TAB-FULL:v23p471/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r9.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r9.claim: Qatāda says God could make the fingers like an animal's hoof, so a person would pick up food only with the mouth.
TAB-FULL:v23p471/r9.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {بلى قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه}

TAB-FULL:v23p473/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r1.claim: Qatāda says God could make the fingers like a camel's hoof or an animal's hoof.
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {على أن نسوي بنانه}

TAB-FULL:v23p473/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk defines banān as the fingers and says God could make them like a camel's hoof.
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r2.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {على أن نسوي بنانه}

TAB-FULL:v23p473/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r3.claim: One grammatical view treats qādirīn as standing for the finite verb “we are able,” recasting that verb as an active participle.
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r3.anchor: فقال بعضهم: نصب لأنه واقع موقع نفعل

TAB-FULL:v23p473/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r4.speaker: بعض نحوي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r4.claim: A Kufan grammarian instead attaches the accusative to an implied break from “collect”: the sense is that God has power over them, more than bone-gathering implies.
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r4.anchor: وكان بعض نحوي الكوفة يقول: نصب على الخروج من نجمع

TAB-FULL:v23p473/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r5.speaker: بعض نحوي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r5.claim: The Kufan grammarian rejects deriving the accusative from “we are able” by changing a finite verb to a participle.
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r5.anchor: وقال: قول الناس بلى نقدر، فلما صرفت إلى قادرين نصبت خطأ

TAB-FULL:v23p473/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r6.speaker: الفرزدق
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r6.claim: The Kufan grammarian cites al-Farazdaq's accusative khārijan as evidence, reading it under an implied vow not to insult or depart from false speech.
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r6.anchor: بقول الفرزدق: على قسم لا أشتم الدهر مسلما

TAB-FULL:v23p473/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r7.speaker: بعض نحوي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r7.claim: A Basran grammarian attaches qādirīn to “We shall gather them”: God will gather them, able to fashion their fingers.
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r7.anchor: وكان بعض نحوي البصرة يقول: نصب على نجمع

TAB-FULL:v23p473/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī judges the Basran analysis the more correct according to Arabic grammar.
TAB-FULL:v23p473/r8.anchor: وهذا القول الثاني أشبه بالصحة على مذهب أهل العربية

TABATABAI:75:1-4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r1.claim: The surah announces the Great Resurrection, describes its signs and human fate, says the journey toward it begins at death, and closes by arguing for resurrection from God's power to originate life; its context marks it Meccan.
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r1.anchor: تنبئ بوقوع يوم القيامة أولا ثم تصفه ببعض أشراطه

TABATABAI:75:1-4/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r10.claim: Bala means that God will gather the bones; qadirin is a circumstantial accusative attached to the implied subject of bala.
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r10.anchor: حال من فاعل مدخول بلى المقدر

TABATABAI:75:1-4/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r11.claim: Banan means the fingertips; another reported definition is the fingers themselves.

TABATABAI:75:1-4/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r12.claim: To make the fingertips even means to recreate their original form, including their remarkable images and structure.
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r12.anchor: وتسوية البنان تصويرها على ما هي عليها من الصور

TABATABAI:75:1-4/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r13.claim: The fingertips are singled out for their intricate forms, structure, and number, which enable countless precise grasping, movements, crafts, and human skills; their markings also reveal new secrets.
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r13.anchor: للاشارة إلى عجيب خلقها بما لها من الصور وخصوصيات التركيب والعدد تترتب عليها فوائد جمة

TABATABAI:75:1-4/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r14.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r14.claim: An alternative says God could make fingers and toes undivided, like a camel's sole or donkey's hoof, depriving people of the many acts enabled by separate digits.
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r14.anchor: وقيل المراد بتسوية البنان جعل أصابع اليدين والرجلين مستوية شيئا واحدا من غير تفريق

TABATABAI:75:1-4/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r15.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r15.claim: He prefers the preceding interpretation of recreating the original, distinct fingertips over making the fingers an undivided surface.
TABATABAI:75:1-4/r15.anchor: من فنون الأعمال، والوجه المتقدم أرجح

AKHFASH:v2p557/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p557/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p557/r1.claim: He explains قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه as being able to gather the bones: بلى نجمعها قادرين.
AKHFASH:v2p557/r1.anchor: قال {بلى قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه} أي: على أن نجمع. أي: بلى نجمعها قادرين

AKHFASH:v2p557/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p557/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p557/r2.claim: The singular of بنان is بنانة.
AKHFASH:v2p557/r2.anchor: أي: على أن نجمع. أي: بلى نجمعها قادرين. وواحد "البنان": بنانة.

TABRISI:75:4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:4/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:4/r2.claim: Qādirīn is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier, with its governing verb omitted and understood from the preceding context; 2:239 supplies a parallel ellipsis.
TABRISI:75:4/r2.anchor: { بلى قادرين } نصب على الحال والتقدير بلى بجمعها قادرين

FARRA:v3p207/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p207/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p207/r4.claim: A tafsir says God can make the fingers solid and undivided like a camel’s hoof; al-Farra explains that God can restore even the smallest bones as they were.
FARRA:v3p207/r4.anchor: جاء في التفسير: بلى نقدر على أن نسوي بنانه، أي: أن نجعل أصابعه مصمتة غير مفصلة كخف البعير، فقال : بلى قادرين على أن نعيد أصغر العظام كما كانت،

FARRA:v3p207/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p207/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p207/r5.claim: The accusative قادرين breaks from نجمع; the sense is “yes, we are able,” with an omitted verb, as in the spoken paraphrases he gives.
FARRA:v3p207/r5.anchor: وقوله: «قادرين» نصبت على الخروج من «نجمع» ، كأنك قلت في الكلام: أتحسب أن لن نقوي عليك، بلى قادرين على أقوى منك.

FARRA:v3p207/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p207/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p207/r6.claim: Nominative is also valid as a new sentence: “Yes, we are able to do more than that.”
FARRA:v3p207/r6.anchor: ولو كانت رفعا على الاستئناف، كأنه قال: بلى نحن قادرون على أكثر من ذا- كان صوابا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p499#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p499#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p499#3/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba refers readers to Kitāb Taʾwīl al-Mushkil for the explanation of this passage about gathering bones, shaping fingertips, and human persistence in sin.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p475#3/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p475#3/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p475#3/r7.claim: The oath’s answer is the passage beginning “Does the human think” and ending “capable.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p475#3/r7.anchor: وجواب القسم في قوله: {أيحسب الإنسان} إلى قوله: {قادرين}.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p475#3/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p475#3/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر النحاس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p475#3/r8.claim: Abu Jaʿfar al-Nahhas instead says the oath’s answer is omitted, with an implied “You will surely be resurrected.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p475#3/r8.anchor: وقال (2) أبو جعفر النحاس: جواب القسم محذوف، على تقدير: (لتبعثن)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p475#3/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p475#3/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p475#3/r11.claim: Bala supplies the implied “We will gather them”; qadirin is a circumstantial accusative governed by that omitted verb, the grammarians’ consensus.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p475#3/r11.anchor: قال الله تعالى: {بلى} (8) أي: بلى نجمعها قادرين. فقوله: (قادرين)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p475#3/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p475#3/r12.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p475#3/r12.claim: Al-Farra rejects the common parse “bala, we are able”: one cannot make qadirin accusative merely by converting a finite verb to an active participle.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p475#3/r12.anchor: قال الفراء: وقول الناس: بلى نقدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God could make the hand like a camel’s hoof or a pig’s cloven hoof.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أن نجعل يده كخف البعير، أو كظلف الخنزير (¬3).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r2.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r2.claim: Muqatil and al-Kalbi say the fingers could be joined into one palm, like a camel’s hoof, useless for delicate tasks in life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل (¬4)، والكلبي (¬5): أن نجعل أصابعه ملتزقة مثل الكف، فيكون كخف البعير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r3.speaker: قتادة وعكرمة والحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r3.claim: Qatada, Ikrima, and al-Hasan similarly explain it as making the fingers like an animal’s hoof.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r3.anchor: وهذا قول قتادة (¬6) # (وعكرمة) (¬1) (¬2)، والحسن (¬3)، قالوا: نجعلها كحافر الدابة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r4.claim: Abu ʿAli al-Farisi explains this as flattening fingers and palm together, removing divisions needed for writing and other delicate work.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r4.anchor: وشرحه أبو علي (الفارسي) (¬5) فقال: بلى قادرين على أن نسوي بنانه أي نجعلها مع كفه كصفيحة مستوية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r5.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r5.claim: Ahmad ibn Yahya cites the oath “By the One who split them five from one,” meaning the fingers from the palm.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r5.anchor: قال أحمد بن يحيى: ومن أيمانهم: لا والذي شقهن خمسا من واحدة (¬9)؛ يريدون الأصابع من الكف.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r6.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r6.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the digits could be made into one shape, opposite the Arab saying that the fingers in the palms are not equal.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r6.anchor: وقال المبرد: أي يجعلها على هيئة واحدة، فيكون على خلاف ما تقول العرب: وما يستوي في الراحتين الأصابع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r7.claim: Abu Ishaq finds the context of gathered bones best: God can restore the fingertips as they were, despite their smallness and decay.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r7.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: والذي هو أشكل بجمع العظام. بلى نجمعها، قادرين على تسوية بنانه على ما كانت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r8.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r8.claim: Abu ʿAli also records this reading as restoring the fingertips to their former state.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r8.anchor: وذكر أبو علي هذا القول، فقال: أي: يردها كما كانت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r9.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r9.claim: Ibn Qutayba says God can rejoin decayed phalanges into fingertips; whoever can do that can more readily gather larger bones.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r9.anchor: وشرح ابن قتيبة هذا القول فقال: هذا رد من الله عليهم، وذلك أنهم ظنوا أن الله لا ينشر الموتى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r10.claim: The Farazdaq line puts kharijan in the accusative by ellipsis after an understood covenant: “I have pledged not to curse anyone, nor to go out.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p478/r10.anchor: علي قسم لا أشتم الدهر مسلما ... ولا خارجا من في زور كلام (¬1) فإنما نصبت (خارجا)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:1-5/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:1-5/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:1-5/r7.claim: God can gather the bones and make the fingertips like a camel's hoof, leaving the person unable to do anything.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:1-5/r7.anchor: بلى قادرين } بلى نقدر على جمعها و { على أن نسوي بنانه } نجعله كخف البعير، فلا يمكنه أن يعمل بها شيئا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:1-5/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:1-5/r8.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:1-5/r8.claim: An alternative says God restores the fingertips to their original form, however fine and small the bones are.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:1-5/r8.anchor: وقيل: نسوي بنانه على ما كانت وإن دقت عظامها وصغرت.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r1.claim: Arab polytheists denied resurrection after bodies decayed to dust and asked how it could happen, though their aim was mockery and denial rather than learning; the verses censure them and affirm resurrection decisively.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r1.anchor: putperest Araplar, insanların öldükten ve bedenleri çürüyüp toprak haline geldikten sonra yeniden diriltilmesini imkânsız görüyor, Hz. Peygamber’e bunun nasıl olacağını soruyorlardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r2.claim: Elsewhere taswiya describes fully giving a person bodily features during creation; see 82:7 and 87:2.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r2.anchor: tesviye kavramı, “yaratılış sürecinde insana bedensel özelliklerinin tam olarak verilmesi” anlamında başka âyetlerde de geçmektedir (bk. İnfitâr 82/7; A‘lâ 87/2).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r3.claim: By this usage, taswiya may mean not only reassembling finger bones but restoring every feature of the fingers completely.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r3.anchor: konumuz olan âyette tesviye kavramının, parmak kemiklerinin bir araya getirilmesi yanında parmaklara bütün özelliklerinin yeniden eksiksiz verileceğini de ifade ettiği düşünülebilir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r4.claim: The unique patterns on palms and fingertips may be a personal identity code; fingers are singled out to point to the fine detail of recreation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r4.anchor: Her bir insanın avuç içinde ve parmak uçlarında bulunan çizgiler, onun bir tür kişilik şifresi olup başka hiçbir insanda bulunmayan, yalnız ona ait olan bir kompozisyonda yaratılmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r5.claim: The verse names the fingers as an eloquent part standing for the whole body.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:3/r5.anchor: edebî bir sanat olarak parmaklar zikredilmiş, fakat bedenin tamamı kastedilmiştir.

TABRISI:75:4-11/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:4-11/r1.speaker: الزجاج والجبائي وأبو مسلم
TABRISI:75:4-11/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj, al-Jubbāʾī, and Abū Muslim say God can restore even the small finger bones and align them; assembling small bones proves He can assemble larger ones all the more.
TABRISI:75:4-11/r1.anchor: ونؤلف بينها حتى يستوي البنان ومن قدر على جمع صغار العظام فهو على جمع كبارها أقدر عن الزجاج والجبائي وأبي مسلم

TABRISI:75:4-11/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:4-11/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
TABRISI:75:4-11/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda alternatively understand that God could make fingers like a hoof or paw, but favored humans with fingertips.
TABRISI:75:4-11/r2.anchor: كالخلف والحافر فيتناول المأكول بفيه ولكنا مننا عليه بالأنامل ليكمل بها المنفعة ويتهيأ له القبض والبسط والارتفاق بالأعمال اللطيفة كالكتابة وغيرها عن ابن عباس وقتادة

TABRISI:75:4-11/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:4-11/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
TABRISI:75:4-11/r3.claim: Fingertips enable grasping, releasing, and fine tasks such as writing.
TABRISI:75:4-11/r3.anchor: ويتهيأ له القبض والبسط والارتفاق بالأعمال اللطيفة كالكتابة وغيرها عن ابن عباس وقتادة

BURHAN:v4p262/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p262/r1.speaker: الجمهور
BURHAN:v4p262/r1.claim: Most take the implied answer as ‘rather, We will resurrect them, fully able,’ since denial calls for an affirmative statement of reassembly.
BURHAN:v4p262/r1.anchor: ثم قال الجمهور التقدير بل نحييها قادرين لان الحساب انما يقع من الانسان على نفي جمع العظام

BURHAN:v4p262/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p262/r2.speaker: الفراء
BURHAN:v4p262/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ supplies ‘then We will surely resurrect them, able’; the author calls this weak because it does not answer in the question’s grammatical pattern.
BURHAN:v4p262/r2.anchor: وقال الفراء التقدير فلنحيها قادرين لدلالة ايحسب عليه وهو ضعيف لانه عدول عن مجئ الجواب على نمط السؤال

BURHAN:v4p262/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p262/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p262/r9.claim: Balā answers the preceding denial that God will gather the bones and rebukes those who think He cannot reassemble them.

BURHAN:v1p373#2/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p373#2/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p373#2/r2.claim: In seven occurrences, stopping at بلى is impermissible because it and what follows form an answer connected to the preceding clause.
BURHAN:v1p373#2/r2.anchor: والثانى ما لا يجوز الوقف عليها لتعلق ما بعدها بها وبما قبلها وذلك فى سبعة مواضع

BURHAN:v4p259/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p259/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p259/r7.claim: Negation and interrogation may be combined in either a literal or figurative question, as shown by these two examples.
BURHAN:v4p259/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يقرن النفى بالإستفهام مطلقا أعم من الحقيقى والمجازى

BURHAN:v3p207/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p207/r6.speaker: سيبويه
BURHAN:v3p207/r6.claim: Sībawayh supplies bلى نجمعها before qādirīn, making it a circumstantial accusative, with the omitted verb indicated by the earlier statement about gathering the bones.
BURHAN:v3p207/r6.anchor: قدره سيبويه ب بلى نجمعها قادرين فقادرين حال

BURHAN:v3p207/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p207/r7.speaker: الفراء
BURHAN:v3p207/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ instead supplies نحسب, guided by the following phrase أيحسب الإنسان.
BURHAN:v3p207/r7.anchor: وقدره الفراء نحسب لدلالة ﴿ أيحسب الإنسان

BURHAN:v3p207/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p207/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p207/r8.claim: The author prefers Sībawayh’s estimate because بلى answers the assertion that God will not gather the bones, not the question whether a human supposes it.
BURHAN:v3p207/r8.anchor: وتقدير سيبويه أولى لأن بلى ليس جوابا ل يحسب

BURHAN:v3p207/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p207/r9.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v3p207/r9.claim: Another proposed estimate is بلى نقدر قادرين.

BURHAN:v3p207/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p207/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p207/r10.claim: The suggestion that qādirīn is accusative simply because it stands in place of a verb is invalid; that is not a recognized cause of accusative case.
BURHAN:v3p207/r10.anchor: وقيل منصوب لوقوعه موقع الفعل وهو باطل لأنه ليس من نواصب الاسم وقوعه موقع الفعل

BURHAN:v3p113/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p113/r5.speaker: الفراء
BURHAN:v3p113/r5.claim: Al-Farra' reads بلى قادرين as an omitted حسبنا قادرين, though the source objects that the stated حساب means conjecture while the implied one would mean knowledge.
BURHAN:v3p113/r5.anchor: وأنكر قول الفراء في قوله تعالى

BURHAN:v3p113/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p113/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p113/r6.claim: The reply defends that analysis by taking the implied حساب as firm belief rather than conjecture, which better matches the expressed wording.
BURHAN:v3p113/r6.anchor: ويجاب بأن الحساب المقدر بمعنى الجزم والاعتقاد لا بمعنى الظن وتقديره بذلك أولى لموافقته الملفوظ

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r7.claim: The author explains the restoration of fingertips as the power to make them like a camel’s hoof, disabling delicate work and showing what fingers enable.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p305/r7.anchor: أي نجعلها كخف البعير فلا تتمكن من الأعمال اللطيفة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p68/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p68/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p68/r5.claim: Although phrased universally, “man” addresses Quraysh deniers of the Judgement; the general address expresses disgust at their attitude.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p69/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p69/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p69/r1.claim: The inner self provides evidence for resurrection, though deniers think decayed bones cannot be gathered; God will restore them in perfect detail, including finger joints.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p69/r1.anchor: These verses assert that the evidence on the Day of Judgement is found within man; one does not have to look in the external world.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p69/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p69/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p69/r2.claim: Bunān means each section of a finger, so restoring them implies that God can rejoin even the smallest joints.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p69/r2.anchor: each of “the sections of a finger”.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p69/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p69/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p69/r3.claim: Qādirīn is an accusative of state (ḥāl) linked to the plural pronoun in najmaʿa.
